transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-08-23
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Mark Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (AuroraLegal - Head of Search), Derek Shaw (AuroraLegal - Eng Manager), Priya Singh (AuroraLegal - Security)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for legal search relevance. Discussed architecture, vector DB options, metrics (MRR/NDCG), security (SOC2/SSO/KMS), and next steps to run pilot benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to walk through Redwood's hosted API for embeddings and the rerank endpoint. I'm Sofia, AE, and Mark our solutions engineer is here to run the demo.
[00:22] Mark: Hi all. Quick agenda — architecture, live demo, how reranking ties into your search stack, and then Q&A. If you have logs or examples it's helpful, Maria I think you shared some sample queries earlier, right?
[00:35] Maria: Yep I dropped a small log sample in the calendar note, um, it's anonymized. We're mostly worried about legal precedence and snippet relevance — so ranking docs correctly for statute queries, commercial and case law.
[00:50] Derek: Our current stack is Elasticsearch + some homegrown cosine reranker, and we also use Pinecone for a portion of embeddings. We're seeing latency spikes during peak ingestion and cost is creeping up.
[01:10] Mark: Cool, that maps to what a lot of legal customers see. For today's demo I'll show hosted embeddings endpoint and a separate rerank endpoint — we surface a candidate set from your vector DB then call Redwood's rerank API for final ordering.
[01:35] Priya: Important — security and data residency. We need to know if any customer text persists in logs, how KMS is used, SOC 2 controls, SSO/SAML support.
[01:50] Sofia: Totally, that's on the list — we'll send the security pack after the call. Our hosted product can be configured with strict retention limits, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS for workspace-level encryption. For SSO we do SAML/Okta and RBAC in the console.
[02:10] Mark: Ok jumping into demo — I'm switching screens. Pardon if some product names are spelled weird in the transcript, the screen share shows the Console.
[02:27] [02:27] Mark: Here is the embeddings API: simple POST to /v1/embeddings with model param, and we return a 768 or 1536-d vector depending on model. We recommend 1536 for legal corpora to capture nuance, but smaller dims can reduce storage and compute.
[03:00] Maria: Do you host the vector DB or do you recommend a partner?
[03:08] Mark: For hosted customers we integrate easily with Pinecone/Weaviate/Chroma — we also provide hosted embeddings + you can store vectors in your DB. Many teams use Redwood embeddings to populate their vector DB, but keep the vector DB in their own cloud.
[03:28] Derek: If we keep vectors locally, how does the rerank flow look?
[03:33] Mark: Typical flow: 1) user query -> dense retrieval from your vector DB -> return top K candidates (K=50) -> call Redwood rerank endpoint with the query and candidate doc snippets -> Redwood returns a score and new ordering. Rerank runs a cross-encoder style model optimized for latency.
[03:55] [03:55] Mark: I'll demo with a small dataset — hitting embeddings API, ingesting into a demo vector store, and then calling rerank.
[04:20] [04:20] Mark: (typing) Here's a sample request body — note we include metadata, chunk ids, and a short snippet. The rerank endpoint accepts either the raw text or cached embedding ids. If you pass embeddings we skip re-embedding which saves time, but both are supported.
[05:00] Maria: How does prefix/KV cache work here? We see a lot of repeated queries across users.
[05:08] Mark: Good question — the hosted runtime has automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts and KV cache for long context. For embeddings and rerank specifically, we have caching for common query hashes which reduces per-request cost. There's also a local TTL you can set from the Console. Sometimes the transcription says 'KV cash' in my notes, sorry.
[05:30] Derek: Latency numbers? Our SLO is 200ms p95 for rerank on a candidate set of 50.
[05:40] Mark: For hosted rerank we typically hit 80–150ms p95 for K=50 on our verified models with 1–2 GPU backends. We can trade off cost by using a smaller cross-encoder or hybrid approach — e.g., initial lightweight re-scoring then full cross-encoder for top 10. Also dedicated capacity can lower variance.
[06:10] Priya: For SOC2 and auditability, do you keep audit logs of rerank calls and model versions? We need to show model versioning for compliance.
[06:20] Sofia: (laughs) my notes say 06: twenty, transcript sometimes messes up numbers. Yes we keep per-request model version metadata, token-level cost breakdown, and you can export audit logs from the Console for a given time range.
[06:40] Maria: What's the expected cost delta if we move from our homegrown reranker to Redwood hosted rerank?
[06:48] Mark: It depends on traffic and K. We provided a sample cost calc in the deck — roughly X tokens per rerank call times per-token price; but more importantly, batching and caching can reduce unit cost dramatically. Our Optimize tool will suggest batch sizes and quantization profiles to hit target cost. We'll run numbers against your logs as a follow-up.
[07:15] [07:15] Mark: Demo: querying local demo index. Query: "precedent for contractual indemnity in commercial leases". Initial vector search results returned 50 candidates. Now calling /v1/rerank with query + candidate snippets.
[07:45] [07:45] Mark: Response back — new ranking, showing higher weight to case summaries that mention "indemnity" in paragraph context and matches for jurisdiction. You can see score deltas.
[08:05] Maria: Nice, the snippet selection looks better than our current ordering. How do you handle hallucination or factual drift in rerank models?
[08:14] Mark: Rerank is safer since it ranks document snippets rather than generating new text. We also have structured output options and guardrails; you can pass trust signals and hard filters — e.g., only rank docs with citation fields, or filter by doc age/residency.
[08:40] Derek: We have PII concerns — client names appear in logs. Can you nuke logs on a per-customer basis?
[08:48] Sofia: Yes, hosted retention policies let you set 0-days retention and we support on-demand deletion for the workspace. For added security you can use Private deployment / VPC where no text leaves your network.
[09:10] Mark: Back to architecture — if you want low variance and dedicated SLA we recommend Dedicated. Hosted gives quick start and managed upgrades. For many customers we run a pilot on hosted, then move to Dedicated or Private if they need VPC + HSM/KMS.
[09:40] Maria: Our immediate goal is to run a 4-week pilot on a subset of logs, measure MRR/NDCG uplift vs baseline. Timeline is Q3. What's typical pilot sizing?
[09:55] Mark: Pilot: 1-2M queries or 100k unique query types across a few verticals, run AB test for reranking. We can run canary traffic and provide dashboards in Console for per-query metrics.
[10:20] [10:20] Mark: Now I'll show the Console for rerank results: per-route latency, per-model cost, token breakdown, and a diffs view to compare before/after rank.
[10:45] Derek: Do you support offline batch reranking for reprocessing older content?
[10:52] Mark: Yes — batched offline rerank jobs are supported. You can schedule re-ranks and we have spot-batch pricing. This is useful for re-indexing with new ranker models.
[11:10] Maria: A question on model explainability — can we see why a doc got a certain score? Some legal reviewers want rationale.
[11:20] Mark: We expose simple saliency signals and feature attributions in the Console — not full LIME-level detail but enough to understand the top terms and token contributions. We also return highlight spans in the rerank response.
[11:45] [11:45] Priya: Encryption at rest — how do you integrate with our KMS?
[11:52] Sofia: We support AWS KMS and GCP CMEK for hosted workspaces. For Private deployments we do customer-managed HSM. We'll include the exact KMS integration docs in the security pack.
[12:10] [12:10] Mark: Quick aside — some customers use a hybrid approach: embeddings and retrieval in their VPC, call Redwood rerank over a private peering link; this gives low-latency and keeps vectors in-customer.
[12:35] Maria: That hybrid model might be attractive.
[12:40] Derek: Any hidden costs for concurrency? We need steady throughput during business hours.
[12:47] Mark: Our Dedicated plan has reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; hosted has soft limits but you can buy throughput packs. We'll surface concurrency and throughput numbers with a recommended configuration after we look at your logs.
[13:15] [13:15] Mark: Now a short detour to embeddings quality — we recommend a model family specifically tuned for legal text; it improves recall for statutes and clause-level semantics. We also test quantized variants that cut cost with small accuracy tradeoffs.
[13:40] Maria: Do you provide embeddings normalization or ann index templates?
[13:45] Mark: Yes — we have recommended ANN index configs for HNSW, Faiss IVF, and parameter suggestions for efConstruction/efSearch. We provide a migration script we can share.
[14:05] Maria: Will the Console show per-doc embedding drift over time?
[14:12] Mark: We have monitoring for embedding space drift and quality checks — Redwood Optimize flags model regressions tied to your eval prompt set.
[14:30] [14:30] Derek: For the rerank model, can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[14:37] Mark: Yes — in the Console you can pin model version per-route, do A/B canary rollouts, and set automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if errors spike.
[15:00] Maria: Are there sample evals for legal use cases?
[15:05] Mark: We ship a sample eval harness and you can bring your own evaluation set. We'll run NDCG/MRR and per-query slices to see where improvements happen.
[15:25] [15:25] Priya: Any third-party audits? SOC2? ISO?
[15:30] Sofia: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified and we can share the latest report under an NDA. ISO plans are in roadmap but SOC2 is current.
[15:45] Maria: Competitors — what do you see folks switching from? Pinecone + homegrown reranker? OpenAI embeddings?
[15:54] Mark: Common combos are Pinecone with in-house re-rankers or using OpenAI embeddings + third-party retrievers. We differentiate by integrated rerank endpoint, cost-aware controls, and the Optimize tooling for batch/caching/quantization.
[16:20] [16:20] Mark: Demo wrap-up — now a quick performance benchmark slide (I switch back to deck): we tested 50-candidate rerank across three models and show p95 latency and per-call token cost.
[16:50] Maria: Looks promising. One more — how do you handle jurisdictional data residency? We sometimes need EU-only processing.
[16:58] Sofia: Hosted has region controls; we have EU regions and can route traffic to those. For strict residency, Private or on-prem is the recommendation.
[17:20] [17:20] Derek: Okay let's talk pilot specifics — target metrics, sample size, owners. Maria and Derek will own evaluation; Sofia/Mark will run pilot setup.
[17:40] Maria: We want to measure NDCG@10 and MRR improvements and track latency impact. We also need a security signoff.
[17:53] Sofia: Great — next steps: I'll send pricing + security docs, Mark will share the benchmark script. We'll propose a pilot plan with milestones and a kick-off meeting for next week.
[18:10] [18:10] Priya: Can you attach the sample security questionnaire we looked at in the RFP? We put an internal note that some fields were missing.
[18:20] Sofia: Yes, we'll attach that and mark items we need to fill out.
[18:30] Derek: Integration complexity — is there a sample code flow for the rerank + vector DB?
[18:35] Mark: We have SDK examples for Python/Node, and a sample repo that shows end-to-end: embed -> upsert to vector DB -> retrieve -> rerank -> present. I'll share link.
[18:50] Maria: What's the expected time to first meaningful result for a pilot?
[18:56] Mark: Usually 1–2 weeks to onboard data and run an initial eval if you can provide sample logs and allow us to use a subset on hosted. If you want VPC then add time for networking.
[19:20] [19:20] Sofia: Quick pricing note — we proposed a pilot credit to offset initial test costs; exact numbers in the email.
[19:40] Maria: Awesome.
[19:45] [19:45] Q&A rapid fire: Derek asks about SDK versions, Mark answers; Priya asks about exfil detection, Sofia confirms DLP hooks and audit logs.
[20:30] [20:30] Mark: I'm going to show one more edge case — when candidate set is noisy we can do relevance re-filtering by metadata before rerank to reduce false positives.
[21:00] Maria: That would help.
[21:10] Derek: Any pitfalls you see during pilots?
[21:15] Mark: Common is mismatched snippet sizes and not normalizing text, which hurts rerank. We usually recommend chunking strategy and canonicalization — we can share a script.
[21:40] [21:40] Sofia: Ok wrapping up, recap of next steps and action owners...
[22:00] [22:00] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll send the security pack, pricing, benchmark script, and proposed pilot plan. Look out for an invite for next week for kick-off.
[22:20] Maria: Thanks, excited to try it.
[22:25] Derek: Thanks all.
[22:30] Priya: Thanks.

End of transcript.

References / links mentioned: deck link (shared in chat), benchmark script repo (will be shared by Mark), security pack (Sofia to attach).
